ex.en: Hirofumi installed fibreglass insulation in the ceiling.
ex.ja: 博文は天井にグラスファイバーの断熱材を入れた。

en: A person who is interned, forcibly or voluntarily.
To imprison somebody, usually without trial.
To confine or hold (foreign military personnel who stray into the state's territory) within prescribed limits during wartime.

intern.ety: From French interner, from interne (“inner, internal”), from Latin internus (“within, internal”), compare Etymology 2.

en: Lacking a sense of responsibility; performed or acting as though without responsibility; negligent.
Someone who is not responsible.

irresponsible.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Italic *n̥-
Latin in-
Latin ir-
English ir-
English responsible
English irresponsible
From ir- + responsible.

ex.en: The man charged me with being irresponsible.
ex.ja: その男は私を無責任だと非難した。

ex.en: It was irresponsible of him to break a promise.
ex.ja: 約束を破るとは彼も無責任だ。

ex.en: It is irresponsible of you to break your promise.
ex.ja: 約束を破るなんて無責任だ。

en: Late.
Last made; hence, made of refuse; inferior.
A gap, a delay; an interval created by something not keeping up; a latency.
Delay; latency.
To fail to keep up (the pace), to fall behind.
To cover (for example, pipes) with felt strips or similar material.

lag.ety: Of unknown origin. Possibly of North Germanic origin.

ex.en: He lags behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: He's lagging behind in science.
ex.ja: 彼は理科で後れをとっている。

ex.en: I've got a bad case of jet lag.
ex.ja: 時差ボケで辛い。

en: One who lends, especially money; specifically, a bank or other entity that specializes in granting loans.

lender.ety: From Middle English lendare, leendare, variants of lenner, lenere, equivalent to lend + -er.

ex.en: That man borrows money from many lenders.
ex.ja: あの男の人は多重債務者である。

ex.en: Money lenders are enjoying a profitable period.
ex.ja: 資金の貸し手は高利益の時期を享受している。

en: The fact or quality of having a position in space.
The features or surroundings of a particular place.

locality.ety: From French localité, from Late Latin localitas, equivalent to local + -ity.

ex.en: The locality does not count for much in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本では土地勘というものは、あまり価値がない。

ex.en: Localities imposed bans on development.
ex.ja: いくつかの地方自治体では開発を禁止した。

en: Something that tempts or attracts, especially one with a promise of reward or pleasure.
An artificial bait attached to a fishing line to attract fish.
To attract by temptation, appeal, or guile.
To attract fish with a lure.

lure.ety: From Anglo-Norman lure, from Old French loirre (Modern French leurre), from Frankish *lōþr, from Proto-Germanic *lōþr-, perhaps ultimately related to *laþō (“invitation, calling”), or from Proto-Indo-European *leh₂- (“to hide”). Compare English allure, also from Old French. Probably related to German Luder (“bait”).

ex.en: The dress lured her into the store.
ex.ja: そのドレスにひかれて彼女はその店の中に入った。

ex.en: He lured her away from her husband.
ex.ja: 彼女を夫の手からおびき出した。

ex.en: He felt the lure of adventure.
ex.ja: 彼は冒険の誘惑を感じた。

en: Intending to do harm; characterized by spite and malice.

malicious.ety: From Middle English malicious, from Old French malicios, from Latin malitiōsus, from malitia (“malice”), from malus (“bad”). Displaced native Middle English ivelwilled and ivelwilly (“malicious”), related to Old English yfelwillende (literally “evil-willing”). By surface analysis, malice + -ious.

ex.en: Please tell me how to deal with malicious comments.
ex.ja: 陰湿な嫌がらせを受けた場合の対処法について教えてください。

ex.en: Beware of 'One Ring' malicious nuisance calls!!
ex.ja: 悪質な迷惑電話、ワンギリにご注意！！

en: A pad on which a person can recline and sleep, usually having an inner section of coiled springs covered with foam or other cushioning ma…
A form of retaining wall used to support foundations or an embankment
To cover with a thick layer, like a mattress; to blanket.

mattress.ety:
Etymology tree
Arabic طَرَحَ (ṭaraḥa)
Arabic مَطْرَح (maṭraḥ)bor.

From Middle English materas, from Old French matras, from Arabic مَطْرَح (maṭraḥ, “place where something is thrown”), from طَرَحَ (ṭaraḥa, “to throw”). Compare divan, from Persian via Turkish (both of Middle Eastern origin, due to the local custom of lying on padding on floor being foreign to Europeans).

ex.en: Do you really hide your money under the mattress?
ex.ja: 本当にマットレスの下にお金隠してるの？

ex.en: I need a new mattress.
ex.ja: 新しいマットレスがいるな。

ex.en: I hid it under the mattress.
ex.ja: マットレスの下に隠しました。

en: A naevus, a pigmented, slightly raised, and sometimes hairy spot on the skin.
To create a network of channels in (waterlogged soil) to improve drainage.

mole.ety:
From Middle English mole, mool, from Old English māl (“a mole, spot, mark, blemish”), from Proto-West Germanic *mail, from Proto-Germanic *mailą (“spot, wrinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *mel-, *melw- (“dark, dirty”), from Proto-Indo-European *mey-, *my- (“to soil, sully”).
Cognate with Scots mail (“spot, stain”), Saterland Frisian Moal (“scar”), German dialectal Meil (“spot, stain, blemish”), Gothic 𐌼𐌰𐌹𐌻 (mail, “spot, blemish”).

ex.en: Mary has a mole under her eye.
ex.ja: メアリーには泣きぼくろがある。

ex.en: That person has a mole at the side of his eye.
ex.ja: あの人は眼の横にほくろがある。

ex.en: I don't think people should make a mountain of a mole hill.
ex.ja: 針ほどのことを棒ほどにいうのはどうかと思います。

en: A government in which sovereignty is embodied within a single, today usually hereditary head of state (whether as a figurehead or as a po…
The territory ruled over by a monarch; a kingdom.

monarchy.ety: From Old French monarchie, from Late Latin monarchia, from Ancient Greek μοναρχία (monarkhía), from μόνος (mónos, “only”) + ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “power, authority”). By surface analysis, mon- (“one, single”) + -archy (“rule, command”).

en: Of, relating to, or connected with muscles.
Brawny, thewy, having strength.

muscular.ety: Late 17th century; from muscle (Latin mūsculus) + -ar. Compare French musculaire.

ex.en: With his muscular constitution he passes for a judoist.
ex.ja: 骨格たくましい体格なので彼は柔道家でとおっている。

ex.en: My muscular strength has weakened from lack of exercise.
ex.ja: 運動不足で筋肉が弱くなった。

ex.en: The bullet penetrated his muscular chest.
ex.ja: 弾丸は彼の厚い胸板を貫通した。
